title: Do International Students Build Trade Networks? A Pre-Specified Structural Gravity Test for OECD and EU Host Countries, 2014–2023
content:
Background: Governments justify international student recruitment by expected economic2
returns, notably stronger trade links with students’ home countries. Cross-sectional studies3
report sizeable student–trade associations, but whether within-pair changes in student4
stocks precede trade changes is unclear. Methods: Combining 377,413 UNESCO records5
of mobile tertiary students with CEPII BACI goods and OECD–WTO services trade, a6
pre-specified Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood gravity model with pair, exporter–year7
and importer–year fixed effects was estimated for 43 OECD and EU hosts and 205 partners8
(2014–2023). Results: The elasticity of host exports with respect to the lagged student9
stock is 0.0109 (pair-clustered SE 0.0081; p= 0.180; 78,753 observations). Pre-specified10
variants give small, mostly insignificant coefficients; stocks measured after the trade year11
predict trade as strongly as lagged stocks, including when all timings share one sample;12
restricting to completely reported pairs or well-covered host-years changes little. Without13
pair fixed effects the coefficient is 17 times larger. Conclusions: No significant association14
could be detected over the period studied, though this does not show that none exists:15
post-graduation networks fall outside this horizon. The cross-sectional association reflects16
persistent pair characteristics. Expected trade gains are a weak basis for programmes such17
as Stipendium Hungaricum, whose overall return this study does not evaluate
